title: Canonical hypercohomology left edge of a natural-indexed complex
statement: Let $B,C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories with derived categories and $G:B\to C$ additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For a cochain complex $K$ indexed by natural numbers and $n\geq0$, extend $K$ by zero to $L$ indexed by integers. Define $\ell_G(K,n):H^n(GK)\to G(H^nK)$ as follows: transport homology to the extension and then to the derived category; apply the derived unit $G(L)\to RG(L)$; apply the left edge of the truncation spectral object for $RG$; identify its target with $G(H^n L)$ using the canonical truncation iso, shift iso and degree-zero right-derived iso; finally transport back to $K$. Every map and comparison is specified by the explicit Lean construction, and no resolution witness is chosen from an existence theorem.
